description: We are a team of three, consisting of two Software Engineering students and one Cybersecurity student. We are passionate about technology, hackathons, and problem-solving.
summary:
NovaVital is a lightweight web dashboard that helps astronauts notice changes in their own health during long space missions. Crew members log sleep, fatigue and mood in under a minute, see seven-day trend charts, and get a plain-language comparison against the previous entry, with a reminder to follow mission protocol. It also visualizes real NASA OSDR data (study OSD-575, SpaceX Inspiration4): immune markers from four astronauts before and after flight.

It addresses the challenge by giving crews a simple tool to gather health indicators and evaluate how they change over time, without needing medical expertise. This matters because on missions to the Moon and Mars, help from Earth is delayed and astronauts must be their own first check. NovaVital is educational and does not diagnose.
details:
Long missions expose astronauts to isolation, radiation, altered gravity and delayed contact with Earth, so the crew must often notice health changes in themselves. NovaVital is a lightweight web dashboard for that daily self-check.

What it does: crew members log sleep hours, fatigue (1-5) and mood (1-5) in under a minute. The app shows 7-day trend charts and a plain-language summary comparing today with the previous entry ("stable" or "needs follow-up"), with general advice to follow mission protocol. A second section plots real NASA OSDR serum immune markers (IL-6, TNF, IL-10) from the four Inspiration4 astronauts before and after flight. Data stays in the user's browser (no server), so it works offline. A "demo data" button adds clearly labeled fictional entries for presentation only.

Benefits and impact: it helps crews notice change over time rather than single readings, and the same approach can support isolated workers on Earth. It is educational and does not diagnose.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no libraries), GitHub Pages for hosting. The NASA CSV was converted to a small JavaScript data file.

Limits and next steps: it tracks subjective indicators only; the NASA data are blood markers (not sleep or mood) from four people, so we draw no statistical conclusions. Next: heart rate, blood pressure, glucose and temperature, personal baselines, and thresholds reviewed by space-medicine experts.
